title: Prudential Regulation Authority Business Plan 2026/27
summary: The PRA Business Plan 2026/27 outlines supervisory priorities for 1,254 regulated firms (686 deposit-takers, 568 insurers), confirming continued focus on safety, soundness, and policyholder protection while implementing Basel III reforms and streamlining supervision. Recent Middle East market turbulence is cited as reinforcing the importance of resilience.
key_points: PRA regulates 1,254 firms: 686 deposit-takers and 568 insurers across all types
Basel III remaining elements implemented in January 2026, with implementation continuing through 2026/27
Simplified capital regime for small domestic banks to be fully in place from January 2027
Work on bank liquidity aims to respond to faster bank runs experienced in US in 2023
Periodic Summary Meetings moving to two-year cycle for all firms
Material headcount reduction of around 140 staff planned for 2026/27
Chief Executive Sam Woods term concludes in June 2026, succeeded by Katharine Braddick
why_it_matters: This business plan signals the PRA's supervisory priorities for UK banks and insurers over the coming year. While primarily an administrative planning document, it indicates regulatory trajectory on capital adequacy, liquidity requirements, and ring-fencing reforms that could affect market participants' operational environment. Direct market impact is limited as the document outlines planned work rather than imminent policy changes.
market_structure_context: The document references liquidity reporting for insurers, bank liquidity requirements in response to faster bank runs (observed mainly in US in 2023), and ring-fencing regime reforms. These touch on financial stability infrastructure but represent supervisory/regulatory policy rather than market microstructure or trading venue operations. Relevance to core market structure topics (trading mechanisms, order flow, market making, execution quality) is tangential.
